paragraphs.text: In the 2004 MG1655 deletion/13C study, aerobic M9 cultures at37°C with5 g/L carbon source supported different physiological roles: PntAB supplied an estimated35–45% of biosynthetic NADPH during glucose growth, while loss of pntAB slowed growth and increased oxidative pentose-phosphate compensation. Soluble UdhA was important on acetate and in a pgi-deficient state with excess NADPH, rather than being required for ordinary glucose growth in that study. Some complementation results were described as data not shown. Crude-extract NADPH/APAD reverse assays measured enzyme capacity, not the same quantity as in-vivo redox flux.

A 2004 redox-linked transcriptional interpretation was later tested more directly: the 2016 study found no correlation of transhydrogenase promoter activities with NADPH pools or formation/consumption fluxes across the tested perturbations. Paraquat at10 µM induced the zwf positive control without inducing pntAB or sthA. This narrows the earlier model under those conditions; it does not assert that every redox perturbation is transcriptionally inert.

Phosphorylated PhoB activates phoA through the exact native regulator→promoter PM00071→transcription-unit TU00052→phoA join. Its reference is P0AFJ5/phoB/b0399,229 residues, with phosphoaspartate53 and phosphorylation-dependent dimer orientation retained in the endpoint. P0A9I3 is GcvR and is explicitly rejected as PhoB. The 2013 acidic/aerobic versus microaerobic findings are available only through the primary abstract and native context, not full-body access. The 2019 phosphate-starvation reporter work used MG1655 promoter fragments, BCD2/msfgfp and pSEVA234/237 plasmids in DH10B resting cells at30°C over0–50 mM phosphate; synthetic Pliar constructs and modeled phosphorylation/feedback rates are separate from measured native-promoter outputs.

Spot42 represses sthA in MG1655-derived strains. The 2011 Northern experiment used NM525 Δspf GS0433 with IPTG-induced pSpot42; the translational-fusion experiment used PM1205 Δspf GS0434 with pBAD sthA-lacZ from its TSS through9–15 codons,0.2% arabinose and ±1 mM IPTG for1 h. The table reports a−4.2±0.5 expression change. RegionIII mutation and compensatory target mutation support direct RNA pairing. The 2012 follow-up discusses multiple pairing regions, including I and III, without establishing simultaneous binding stoichiometry. Its nanC structural probing and Hfq-deletion experiments are not transferred to sthA; the sthA Hfq context in the earlier table retains that earlier source’s evidence level.
